desc:
You have n coins and want to lay them out as a staircase. Row 1 takes one coin, row 2 takes two coins, row 3 takes three, and so on; row k takes k coins. A row is only counted if it is filled completely.

Return the number of complete rows you can build with the n coins.
hints: Building k complete rows costs exactly 1 + 2 + ... + k coins. Do you know a closed form for that sum?
The cost k(k+1)/2 grows with k, so the question "can I afford k rows?" is true for small k and false for large k.
Binary search the largest k with k(k+1)/2 ≤ n. The answer is below 65,536 for every allowed n, so use hi = 65,536; take care that intermediate products do not overflow 32 bits.
editorial: Subtracting 1, 2, 3, ... from n until the next row no longer fits is correct but needs about √(2n) steps, around 65,000 for the largest input. That is fine here, but binary search makes it logarithmic and generalizes to much larger limits.

Row counts are monotone: if k rows are affordable then so are k - 1. Search the largest k in [0, 65535] such that k(k+1)/2 ≤ n. Since k(k+1) can reach about 4.3 billion, do the arithmetic in a 64-bit type (or compare k(k+1)/2 carefully) in languages with 32-bit integers. The closed form floor((sqrt(8n + 1) - 1) / 2) also works but needs a careful integer square root.
